contentBlocks.body:
**Objective.** Run the same built app with a persistent data volume and observable health endpoints.

This is a real project lab in projects/inventory-desk, also available from the Projects page as a source download. Work in an isolated copy of the reference project so you can compare your change with a known baseline. Read Dockerfile; compose.yaml; InventoryDesk.Api/Program.cs before editing. Trace one request from the UI or test through the boundary that owns the behavior.

contentBlocks.code:
docker compose up --build
# In another terminal:
curl http://127.0.0.1:5080/health/ready

contentBlocks.body:
**Acceptance criteria.** The container serves the UI and API, readiness verifies a database connection, and restarting the service retains products in the named volume.

**Make a meaningful variation.** Add your own orchestration health probe to /health/ready and verify its failure when the database becomes unavailable in a disposable environment. Write the observable expectation before editing the implementation. If the variation exposes a defect, keep the smallest failing fixture as a regression test.
Review rubric: The final image runs as a nonroot user, runtime data is outside the image, and a successful process start is not confused with readiness.

**Explain the boundary.** What must survive replacing the container image? Describe both a successful case and a rejected or missing-data case. Compare actual output with the acceptance criteria, including status codes, persisted values, and user-visible feedback where relevant.

**Evidence to keep.** Save the focused test result, a short before/after diff, and a note explaining one tradeoff. Completing the quiz records this lesson's concepts; it does not run the companion checks or certify that the project milestone is finished.
